newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 1996/97 sugar output to drop on bad weather.
newsitem.headline: Japan 1996/97 sugar output to drop on bad weather.

text.p: Japan's sugar production in the 1996/97 sugar year (October/September) is expected to drop 15 percent from a year ago to 716,000 tonnes, due to bad weather in crop growing areas, the Agriculture Ministry said on Friday.
It also said that sugar output in the July-September period of this year would fall by 64 percent from a year earlier to 7,100 tonnes.
Sugar is grown mainly in Hokkaido, in northern Japan, and on the southern island of Okinawa.

"The sugar fields in Okinawa were hit by typhoons and drought last year, and cold weather hit Hokkaido. Domestic sugar output this year will certainly drop," said Yasuo Sasaki, deputy director of the ministry's sugar and starch division.
But he said Japan's sugar imports were unlikely to rise despite the reduced domestic production, due to gradually falling sugar consumption in Japan.
